newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes assume weaker stance on supply glut.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes assume weaker stance on supply glut.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes marked another session of softening differentials for sweet and sour grades on sentiment both markets are well-supplied.
Traders said sour grades continued to mark the most obvious losses, selling some 15-20 cents lower than late Monday. Sweet grades lost around 5-10 cts as well.
"The weaker numbers in the sour grades are doable, since there are as many barrels as you want out there," said a cash trader in Texas.
Foreign supplies of West African crudes have worked to keep Louisiana and Texas sweets under pressure, traders said.

Numbers from late Tuesday showed April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gaining ground after the NYMEX settlement to track around $20.80-90 per barrel. April NYMEX futures had ended 41 cts higher at $20.66.
The supportive trend was mainly based on fresh inventory data, and before that from technical buying, traders said.

Statistics from the American Petroleum Institute (API) gave the late U.S. crude market a bullish tint, with crude reported down 7.62 million barrels for week-ended February 28, against forecasts for a 1-4 million barrel build.
Meanwhile, gasoline stocks were down 1.3 million barrels, distillates up 603,000 barrels and refinery runs inched 0.2 percent lower to 88.6 percent.
On the grade side of business, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ranged around a 14 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing late in the day, after trading earlier at a 10 cts premium.
West Texas Sour/Midland was talked late at a $2.65-75 discount to the WTI/Cushing, after trading as weak as a $2.80 discount to the marker.
April Postings Plus was steady at $2.00-01, traders said.
